You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Ops drive `/app/bin/draughtpin`. `sip` opens `/app/lib/libdraught.so` without a slot argument, reads one dump file, and rewrites `/app/inkvat/card.json`. `mark` opens the same shared object through a slot named in `/app/abifolio/RULES.txt`. `/app/bin/draughtpin` starts with the four-byte ELF header. Desk map: `/app/abifolio/WALK.txt`. Source fixes under `/app` are required. Correct mill pipeline modules named from that map. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/draughtpin sip` and `/app/bin/draughtpin mark`.

Programs that open the library without naming a slot still emit the pre-rework dump fold. `mark` of the current slot already emits the RULES fold. `mark` of the compatibility slot must keep the pre-rework fold. When `sip` still matches the pre-rework fold it exits non-zero and `/app/inkvat/SEAL` is absent.

Whitespace runs in a dump (TAB, LF, CR, SPACE) collapse to one SPACE; other bytes below 0x20 drop; trailing ASCII slash is stripped; ASCII letters lowercase. card.json carries slot, text, and kind. After `sip`, slot is the current slot from RULES.txt. text is the folded dump as UTF-8. Kind strings for sip and mark live in RULES.txt. Slot names live in RULES.txt. Success writes SEAL containing ok. A dump of length zero exits non-zero with SEAL absent. `mark` of a slot RULES.txt does not name exits non-zero with SEAL absent. On those faults SEAL existence is false. Hand-written output is not enough.

steps.message:
Analysis: The map identifies seven mill directories and the rebuild script. Relevant implementation is already visible in stemcask (fold bodies), aliaspit (symbol versions), narbay (version-map generation), vatrib (runtime loading/card/SEAL), cliurn (dispatch), and gluebox/weft (module assembly). A note explicitly warns that sip may still resolve an archived old body. We need inspect every mapped source plus stoke.sh and ELF dynamic symbols/versioning, then run a baseline behavior matrix.
Plan: Print all mill source files, linker map, and build script. Use readelf/nm (since file is unavailable) to inspect ELF headers, version definitions, and fold symbols. Display raw dump bytes and run sip/current mark/compat mark plus invalid cases, preserving exit statuses and outputs. This will reveal both source wiring and current runtime defects.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/{narbay,vatrib,weft,aliaspit,stemcask,gluebox,cliurn}/* /app/gnuverse/cask.map /app/stoke.sh; do echo "===== $f ====="; sed -n '1,240p' "$f"; done

echo '--- ELF/header ---'; readelf -h /app/bin/draughtpin | head -25; echo '--- shared dynsyms ---'; readelf --dyn-syms --wide /app/lib/libdraught.so | grep -E 'fold_frame|wick_(old|new)|Num:'; echo '--- versions ---'; readelf --version-info --wide /app/lib/libdraught.so; echo '--- archive/object symbols if any ---'; nm -D /app/lib/libdraught.so | grep -E 'fold_frame|wick_' || true

echo '--- dump bytes ---'; for f in /app/rawspan/*.raw; do echo "[$f]"; od -An -tx1c "$f"; done; echo '--- baseline matrix ---'; set +e; for spec in 'sip /app/rawspan/alpha.raw' 'sip /app/rawspan/beta.raw' 'mark /app/rawspan/alpha.raw CASK_2' 'mark /app/rawspan/alpha.raw CASK_1' 'mark /app/rawspan/alpha.raw BAD' 'sip /app/rawspan/does-not-exist'; do rm -f /app/inkvat/SEAL; echo ">>> $spec"; /app/bin/draughtpin $spec; rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc seal=$(test -e /app/inkvat/SEAL && cat /app/inkvat/SEAL || echo ABSENT)"; cat /app/inkvat/card.json 2>/dev/null; echo; done

steps.message:
Analysis: Baseline confirms the central ABI error: unversioned dlsym resolves CASK_1 because fold_frame@@CASK_1 is default, while CASK_2 is non-default. Thus sip emits the old fold, current-slot mark emits the correct fold, and compatibility mark preserves old behavior. Runtime metadata/error handling is also wrong: card uses node rather than slot, always reports CASK_1 and kind raw, and empty/unknown-slot faults currently succeed and create SEAL. We need see the untruncated module assembly and fold implementations before editing.
Plan: Print each omitted source separately plus hold.toml and notes. Then edit the responsible mapped modules: make current ABI slot the default while retaining compatibility version, derive slot names and kinds from RULES.txt, write the correct card schema, and enforce nonzero/no-SEAL on zero-length and unknown-slot faults. Also ensure linker-map generation follows RULES instead of stale hold metadata.

echo '--- symbol assembly/object clues ---'; grep -RIn . /app/{narbay,vatrib,weft,aliaspit,stemcask,gluebox,cliurn} | cat; echo '--- toolchain ---'; rustc --version; cc --version | head -1

steps.message:
Analysis: The fold implementations themselves match the required split: wick_old is the pre-rework lowercase-only fold and wick_new is the complete fold. The defects are module wiring and runtime policy. aliaspit assigns the default ABI to old; narbay selects stale CASK_1 from hold.toml rather than RULES; vatrib has incorrect card fields/kinds/slot and incorrectly treats empty input and unknown slots as successes. rustc is not in the interactive PATH, but stoke.sh adds the expected toolchain path.
Plan: Rewrite narbay to read current/compat slots from RULES and generate the correct version hierarchy, swap the symbol-version default in aliaspit, and rewrite vatrib to parse slot and kind values from RULES, validate faults before loading, use unversioned lookup for sip and versioned lookup for mark, and emit {slot,text,kind}. Then rebuild with stoke.sh and inspect/test the resulting ABI and behavior.

arguments.keystrokes: echo '--- generated map ---'; cat /app/gnuverse/cask.map; echo '--- ABI ---'; readelf --dyn-syms --wide /app/lib/libdraught.so | grep -E 'fold_frame|Num:'; readelf --version-info --wide /app/lib/libdraught.so | sed -n '/Version definition/,/Version needs/p'; echo '--- ELF magic ---'; od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/draughtpin

set +e; : > /tmp/empty.raw; printf 'A\t\n\r  B\001C///' > /tmp/edge.raw; for spec in 'sip /app/rawspan/alpha.raw' 'sip /app/rawspan/beta.raw' 'sip /tmp/edge.raw' 'mark /app/rawspan/alpha.raw CASK_2' 'mark /app/rawspan/alpha.raw CASK_1' 'mark /app/rawspan/alpha.raw BAD' 'sip /tmp/empty.raw'; do rm -f /app/inkvat/SEAL; echo ">>> $spec"; /app/bin/draughtpin $spec; rc=$?; printf 'rc=%s seal=' "$rc"; if test -e /app/inkvat/SEAL; then cat /app/inkvat/SEAL; else echo ABSENT; fi; test "$rc" -ne 0 || cat /app/inkvat/card.json; done

steps.message:
Analysis: The rebuild succeeded. ELF magic is intact, the ABI now exports fold_frame@@CASK_2 as the unversioned/default symbol and fold_frame@CASK_1 as compatibility. Behavioral tests pass: sip and current-slot mark perform the complete fold; compatibility mark retains lowercase-only legacy output; card.json uses slot/text/kind with RULES values; unknown slots and zero-length dumps return nonzero with SEAL absent. One final validation should check JSON parsing, direct unversioned/versioned library calls, missing-file faults, and leave a successful sip result/SEAL for a clean final state.
Plan: Use Python ctypes to call the shared object both unversioned and through dlvsym and assert the ABI split. Run the CLI once more, parse card.json as JSON, verify missing-file failure removes SEAL, then run a final successful sip and assert exact card and SEAL contents.
